highlight-about: Who I am and what I focus on.
contact-title: Let’s connect and build something useful.
contact-text: I am always open to conversations about cloud infrastructure, systems engineering, and practical projects where I can learn and contribute.
section-about-intro: My name is Tommy Quatretemps. I am a systems and network management student with a strong interest in low-level programming and systems-oriented software development. I am especially motivated by technology that sits close to the hardware, where performance, efficiency, and correctness are central.
section-about-workstyle: In how I work, I value structure and clarity. I do best in environments where expectations and ways of working are clearly defined. I am strongly execution-focused and analytical, and I prefer not to rush decisions, because I want to avoid mistakes deliberately. Although rapid, abrupt changes can sometimes challenge me, I can adjust my pace when the situation requires it.
section-about-teamwork: In a team I am cooperative and engaged, without needing to take a lead role. In social settings I am rather reserved, especially in new contexts, but in a trusted environment I communicate openly and constructively. Combined with a critical mindset, this lets me contribute in a stable, positive way on teams where I feel at home.
section-about-technical: Technically, I currently have a solid baseline. I can build complex cloud infrastructures, have experience with application development, and a reasonably strong grounding in cybersecurity. That breadth helps me not only build systems, but also evaluate them critically for security and reliability.
section-about-ambition: In the coming years I want to work where I can create real technical value. I aim to specialize further in low-level development, with a clear focus on C, C++, and assembly. A key learning goal is to understand assembly deeply and apply it to analyze and optimize code with attention to performance. I want to build software that is technically sound, efficient, and clearly useful.
section-seminars-desc: This section lists seminars and workshops I attended.
seminar-gluo-desc: A seminar on multi-cloud where we used Gluo hands-on labs to set up a multi-cloud infrastructure across AWS and Azure.
seminar-toreon-desc: A seminar on ethical hacking that explained how we could find our first CVE and included several CTF challenges.
seminar-police-desc: A seminar where police cases were presented to demonstrate their methods and the type of work they perform.
seminar-cegeka-desc: A seminar on the nuances of configuring efficient, secure and scalable networks in Azure cloud.
seminar-brightest-title: Brightest: Pentesting — break in to secure (SNB)
seminar-brightest-desc: A seminar where we learned the basics of penetration testing.
seminar-secwise-title: Secwise: Cyber security with a focus on identity (SNB/all)
seminar-secwise-desc: A seminar on how identity plays a central role in cybersecurity.
seminar-gluo-devsecops-desc: A seminar on how we as developers can bring security into our DevOps workflows.
seminar-cegeka-dc-desc: A visit to Cegeka’s data center to see how a facility like this looks and operates on the inside.
section-innovation-desc: Innovation track (Security & Cloud), workshops, and hackathon-style security challenges.
innovation-exclusive-title: Innovation track — Exclusive Networks: firewalls (Security & Cloud)
innovation-exclusive-desc: Hands-on work with firewalls and different configuration setups.
innovation-resilix-desc: We covered cyber attacks, ransomware, and incident response, then worked through a practical case. My group placed second and won tickets to BSides Limburg.
innovation-hackathon-title: Hackathon: Cyber Security Challenge Belgium 2025 (Online Qualifiers)
innovation-hackathon-desc: A security competition for higher-education students featuring challenges in cryptography, reverse engineering, network analysis, web & mobile security, and forensic investigation. Participation: Team (Backdoor Boys).
innovation-hackathon-location: Online via the CTF platform of Cyber Security Challenge
innovation-hackathon-2026-title: Hackathon: Cyber Security Challenge Belgium 2026 (Online Qualifiers)
innovation-hackathon-2026-desc: A security competition for higher-education students featuring challenges in cryptography, reverse engineering, network analysis, web & mobile security, and forensic investigation. Participation: Solo.
innovation-hackathon-2026-location: Online via the CTF platform of Cyber Security Challenge

section-internationalization-desc: Cross-border learning and community events outside the regular curriculum.
internationalization-fosdem-desc: FOSDEM is an annual two-day conference in Brussels on free and open-source software. Developers from around the world share talks, workshops, and projects.
internationalization-berlintrip-desc: Study trip to Germany focused on higher education, industry innovation, and local tech communities.
internationalization-berlintrip-bielefel: Visit to a university of applied sciences where we gained insight into their programmes, operations, and international collaborations.
internationalization-berlintrip-hannover: Visit to one of the world’s largest industrial trade fairs, with a focus on technological innovations and trends in industry and automation.
internationalization-berlintrip-berlin-d: Cultural exploration of the city combined with a meeting with the
, where we got to know the local tech and hacker community.
section-personalProject-desc: Projects I built in my spare time to learn, experiment or solve interesting problems.
personal-k3s-desc: A simple ansible script that autonomously sets up an k3s cluster. I see it as a finished project.
personal-bookwriter-desc: A client-side Minecraft Fabric mod: run .write in chat to fill writable books from your inventory, with titles, automatic splitting across volumes, and async signing so the game stays responsive.
personal-ytshorts-desc: A lightweight Firefox add-on that hides YouTube Shorts shelves and suggestions with simple injected CSS.
personal-http-desc: A small C HTTP server I wrote to learn the language—Makefile build, serves a sample index.html, and keeps the scope realistic rather than RFC-complete.
personal-homelab-desc: I run a homelab on Proxmox for virtualization and workloads, and I host Jenkins there for builds and automation.
